title: Adjoint chain maps on restriction kernels: maps and homotopies
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites with abelian sheaf categories [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a functor whose precomposition sends abelian sheaves to abelian sheaves, and let $R:\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ be $R(G)(W)=G(uW)$, and suppose $L\dashv R$ is an additive adjunction [def-sp-left-exact-additive], with $L$ preserving kernels and cokernels. Here an adjunction means natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(LF,G)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,RG)$; bounded below means the terms are zero in all sufficiently negative degrees. Let $m:V\to T$ and $m':V'\to T'$ be monomorphisms in the two sites, and let $t:T'\to uT$ and $s:V'\to uV$ satisfy $u(m)\circ s=t\circ m'$. For a sheaf cochain complex $I$ on $\mathcal C$ set $A_m(I)=\ker(I(T)\to I(V))$ degreewise and write $D_m(I)$ for its diagram $A_m(I)\to I(T)\to I(V)$, with inclusion and restriction. Use integer-indexed complexes and the derived localization $Q$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

(1) For complexes $I,J$ on $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ and a chain map $h:LI\to J$, let $b:I\to RJ$ be its degreewise adjoint. The maps $I(T)\xrightarrow{b_T}J(uT)\xrightarrow{J(t)}J(T')$ and $I(V)\xrightarrow{b_V}J(uV)\xrightarrow{J(s)}J(V')$ commute with restriction. They induce a unique map $A_m(I)\to A_{m'}(J)$ compatible with the inclusions, and together give a morphism $D_m(I)\to D_{m'}(J)$.

(2) If $h-h'=d_Jz+z\,d_{LI}$ for degree $-1$ sheaf maps $z$, the degreewise adjoints of $z$, evaluated and restricted along $t,s$, give compatible homotopies on the three components of these diagram maps. In particular the map on kernel complexes is homotopy invariant. If $I,J$ are bounded-below complexes of injective abelian sheaves [def-sp-injective-resolutions], every derived morphism $a:Q(LI)\to QJ$ has such a representative $h$, unique up to homotopy, and the induced maps on the three cohomology groups depend only on $a$. These cohomology maps are unchanged under the canonical identifications obtained by replacing $I,J$ with other bounded-below injective representatives of the same derived objects.
